note: In der Herde bist du ein geschwätziges Gnu. Allein suchst du laut Profil instinktiv dichten Wald und tarnst dich im Unterholz. Das ist das Okapi, die Waldgiraffe. Vom Gnu bleibt nur die Unruhe, die dich zu anderen Pflanzenfressern treibt.

analogs.covers: Solo life: the shy forest giraffe that hides in dense woodland and browses unseen
Restlessness: uneasy alone, it tags along with other herbivores until it finds a herd again

solo.headline: A lone okapi in a sauropod's body: the shy forest giraffe that hides in thick woodland, tags along with any friendly herbivore and uses bigger sauropods as a shield.

setting.label: Dense woodland, close to any sauropod it can find
setting.note: A solitary Amargasaurus hides in dense woodland like the woods it hatched in, and joins other herbivores or sauropods it meets along the way.

solo.playsLike: Alone you instinctively seek out dense woodland like the place you hatched in, where close-packed trees and thick undergrowth hide you from predators. You are uneasy without a herd and gladly accept the company of other herbivore species until you reunite with a sauropod group. If another sauropod is near, you keep it between you and the predator as a meat-shield; if none is near, you rear your head and whip your tail anxiously. You don't chase fleeing predators, but you may charge to drive them off and then back away, and you move to a more defensible spot when you can. You still flee Allosaurus and Torvosaurus.

why.text: “When traveling alone, Amargasaurus instinctively seek out dense woodlands”, where trees and undergrowth give it camouflage. Okapis live hidden in dense rainforest.
A loner “may attract the company of other herbivore species” and enjoys it until it finds a sauropod group again, as a stray wildebeest joins zebras.
Alone it may use another sauropod species “as a meat-shield if they are available”, keeping the bigger animal between itself and the predator.
It does not chase fleeing predators, but “may charge to drive them away from them, backing off once they retreat”.
Amargasaurus are “uneasy when alone and require constant reassurance of their herd's presence”. The okapi's solitude is its own choice; this one only puts up with it.

notLike: Okapis are content alone; a lone Amargasaurus is anxious and always looking for a herd.
Okapis never leave the forest; Amargasaurus still travels the sauropod routes to its nesting grounds.
solo.summary: Solo bist du kein Gnu in der Herde, sondern ein Okapi: die scheue Waldgiraffe, die sich im dichten Wald versteckt. Allein zieht es dich instinktiv in dichtes Gehölz wie das, in dem du geschlüpft bist, denn zwischen eng stehenden Bäumen und im Unterholz sieht dich kein Räuber. Ganz wohl ist dir allein nie: Du schließt dich gern anderen Pflanzenfressern an, bis du wieder zu Sauropoden findest. Ist ein anderer Sauropode in der Nähe, hältst du ihn zwischen dir und dem Räuber. Ist keiner da, wirst du nervös, reckst den Kopf und peitschst mit dem Schwanz. Fliehenden Räubern jagst du nicht nach, du scheuchst sie höchstens kurz weg. Vor Allosaurus und Torvosaurus fliehst du immer.
